Filled in automatically when it can be worked out; a save under {folder} often has nothing to work it out from, so you can set it here.

game.appId.unreachable: Couldn't reach Steam to check this number. If Steam's store or CDN is blocked on this network, cover art won't load here either — the ID itself may well be right.

game.branches.footnote: Switching branches snapshots your current save first, then restores the other branch's latest state. A branch you just created has no state of its own yet, so it starts from whatever is in your save folder now — the two diverge from the first snapshot you take on it.
game.branches.hint: A branch is a separate line of saves — a second playthrough, or a run you want to keep apart from your main one. You'll be asked what it starts from.

game.header.missing.body: It may have been moved or deleted, or be on a drive that isn't connected. Nothing is snapshotted or synced for this game until it's back — OpenSave picks it up again within a minute. If the save lives somewhere else now, point the game at it with Edit.
game.header.missing.title: This save folder is not there.
game.header.notFoundHint: Steam on this PC does not have it, and it is in no folder games are kept in. Set its program under Configuration to launch it from somewhere else.
game.header.openFolderTitle: Show this folder in your file manager
game.ignore.empty: This game's folders are empty, so there is nothing to pick yet.
game.ignore.intro: Some games keep device-specific settings in the same folder as the save, and copying those to another machine can break the game there. List them here and they stay put: never sent, never received, never deleted by a sync.
game.ignore.severalFolders: A pattern applies to {every}, so a name that appears in two of them is excluded in both.
game.ignore.severalFoldersStrong: every one of this game's folders
game.ignore.snapshots: {captured}, so a restore brings them back — excluding something stops it travelling, it never stops it being backed up.
game.ignore.syntax: One pattern per line, like a {gitignore} — {byName} by name, {top} only at the top, {ext} by extension, {folder} for a whole folder, {exception} for an exception. Case doesn't matter. Set the same list on your other devices; each one applies its own.
game.ignore.tickHint: Ticking a file writes the pattern for you, anchored so it can only ever mean that one file. Unticking a file caught by a wildcard adds a {bang} exception rather than deleting the wildcard.
game.ignore.title: Files that shouldn't sync
game.link.otherDevicesNote: Nothing is removed on either device
game.link.thisDeviceNote: Its entry here merges into this one
game.locations.intro: Some games keep their save split across more than one folder — the save data in one place, settings or mods in another. Add each extra folder here and it is synced, snapshotted and restored along with the main one.
game.locations.removed: The “{name}” folder is no longer covered. Its files are left where they are.
game.locations.sameName: Give the same {name} on your other devices — that is what the two sides match on, since the folder lives somewhere different on each machine. Removing a location here never deletes its files.
game.locations.title: Save locations
game.locations.unmapped: no folder on this device — this location isn't being synced

game.manage.linkRemoteConfirm: Link "{other}" on {device} to "{name}"? The two will be treated as the same game when these devices sync. Nothing on either device is removed.
game.manage.linkedIntro: If this game is tracked under a different name or drive on another PC (e.g. a Steam copy vs. a portable copy), link the copies so their saves sync across devices. Linking merges another tracked game here into this one: its save files stay where they are, and its snapshots move here, onto a branch named after it.
game.manage.nothingToLink: Nothing to link to. Track the other copy on this device, or pair the device that has it and make sure it's online — its games appear here once it answers.
game.manage.stopTrackingDesc: Removes "{name}" from OpenSave. Your save files and existing snapshot archives on disk are kept.
game.newBranch.copyDesc: "{name}" begins exactly where you are now. The two only diverge from the first snapshot you take on it — so this is the one for trying something without losing your place.
game.newBranch.copyTitle: A copy of my current save
game.newBranch.freshDesc: "{name}" begins empty, for a new playthrough from scratch. Switching to it clears your save folder — your current save is snapshotted first and comes straight back when you switch to {branch}.
game.newBranch.hint: Either way nothing is lost. Switching between branches snapshots whatever is in your save folder first, and refuses to change anything if that snapshot can't be taken.
game.newBranch.question: What should it start from?
game.newBranch.title: New branch — {name}

internet.allEncryptedMany: Saves to all {count} of your devices here are encrypted — nobody else in this room can read them.
internet.allEncryptedOne: Saves to your other device here are encrypted — nobody else in this room can read them.
internet.connectingHint: Free-hosted relays can take up to a minute to wake from sleep — hang tight, we retry automatically.
internet.lead: Sync across the internet with no port forwarding: both devices join the same room code on a relay, and the connection to it is encrypted. The relay stores nothing — no copy of a save is written to it.
internet.noneEncryptedMany: Saves sent through this room are {notEncrypted}, so anyone holding this room code can read them. Pair those devices again to fix it.
internet.noneEncryptedOne: Saves sent through this room are {notEncrypted}, so anyone holding this room code can read them. Pair “{name}” again to fix it.
internet.notInRoomHint: Enter a room code below and press {button} to start syncing over the internet.
internet.pairHereEncrypted: Devices you pair here sync encrypted end to end, so nobody else holding this code — including the relay — can read your saves. Both devices need this version; each one shows its own state here and under Devices once it's paired.
internet.relayHint: Run your own with the opensave-relay binary and point this at it.
internet.relayLocked: Set by the {variable} environment variable, so it can't be changed here. Change the variable and restart OpenSave, or unset it to go back to the saved setting.
internet.repairNote: Both devices need a recent version for this, and internet pairings made before it need to be made again: pairing over a relay never kept the key, so an older pair still sends in the clear. Unpair and pair those two devices again to protect them. Pairings made over a local network kept their key and are unaffected.
internet.roomCodeLabel: Room code — share this with your other device
internet.roomEmpty: No other devices in the room yet. Enter the same code on your other device and it will appear here.
internet.someEncryptedMany: {encrypted} of {total} paired devices here are encrypted. Pair the others again to protect them too.
internet.someEncryptedOne: {encrypted} of {total} paired devices here are encrypted. Pair the other one again to protect it too.
internet.trust: Saves are sealed between your two devices, so the relay passes on data it cannot read — not even ours. It can still see that two devices are talking, roughly how much data moves, and which games by id. Running {link} keeps that from us too.
internet.waiting: Waiting for your other device to join with the same code.

locationConflict.decideLaterHint: Nothing of this folder syncs until you decide. Open the game to decide.
locationConflict.desc: This is one of {game}'s extra save folders, and it changed on both this device and {peer}. The game's main save is unaffected and keeps syncing; only this folder is waiting on you.
locationConflict.hint.choices: A snapshot of every one of this game's folders is taken before either choice is applied, so both are undoable from the Snapshots tab. {keepMine} makes this device's copy the shared one and asks {peer} to take it — {peer} gets its own say if it has newer work. {useTheirs} brings their copy here.
locationConflict.hint.noKeepBoth: There is no “keep both” for a folder: that option puts the other copy on a branch, and branches cover the whole game rather than one of its folders.
locationConflict.notify.body: Its “{root}” folder differs on both devices — choose which to keep.

protection.detail.direct: This device is reached straight over your local network, so nothing passes through a relay. Local traffic is not encrypted, so treat an untrusted network accordingly.
protection.detail.open: Saves sent to this device over the internet can be read by anyone holding your room code, including whoever runs the relay. Pairing over a relay did not keep an encryption key in older versions. Unpair and pair these two devices again to fix it.
protection.detail.pending: The key is in place. Encryption starts as soon as this device checks in, which usually takes a few seconds.
protection.detail.sealed: Saves sent to this device are sealed between the two of you. The relay — and anyone else holding your room code — passes them on without being able to read them.
protection.fingerprint: Pairing fingerprint {fingerprint} — it should read the same on the other device.
restore.compareFailed: Couldn't compare it with your save first ({error}). Restoring is still safe.
restore.identical: Your save already matches this snapshot — restoring it would change nothing.
restore.safe: Your current save is kept as a snapshot first, so this can be undone.
restore.title: Restore this snapshot?
restore.unplaced: It also has files for {names}, which has no folder on this device; they are left out.

settings.checks.checkNowHint: Each is read back in full and every file compared with its checksum. A snapshot is also checked before it is restored.
settings.checks.damagedExplain: Their archives were deleted or damaged outside OpenSave. Every other snapshot is fine, and so is each game's save.
settings.checks.firstSoon: The first a little after OpenSave starts.

settings.checks.removeConfirm.other: Remove the {n} snapshots that can't be restored from the history? Their archives are already gone or damaged, so nothing that could be restored is lost; every other snapshot stays.

settings.checks.removed.other: Removed {n} snapshots that couldn't be restored

settings.checks.repairHint: With cloud backup on, each snapshot was uploaded as it was taken: a whole copy there is fetched, checked and put back. What has no copy anywhere can only be removed — the record promises a save that no longer exists.
settings.checks.scheduleHint: {first} Anything the cloud still has whole is put back as it's found.
settings.checks.stillChecked: Snapshots are still checked before they're restored.

settings.reset.confirm.one: Untrack all {n} game? They'll be removed from your library so you can re-add them from the correct locations. Your save snapshots on disk are kept — nothing is deleted.
settings.reset.confirm.other: Untrack all {n} games? They'll be removed from your library so you can re-add them from the correct locations. Your save snapshots on disk are kept — nothing is deleted.

settings.reset.hint: Untrack every game at once, then scan again to add them back from the correct locations — useful after moving games between launchers or drives. This only clears the tracking list; your save snapshots on disk are kept.
settings.reset.title: Reset tracking
settings.scanner.excludeFolderTitle: Choose a folder to exclude from scans
settings.scanner.excludeHint: Scans skip these folders and everything inside them — handy for stale save locations (like an old GSE saves directory) you don't want offered again.
settings.scanner.extraFoldersHint: Scanning already checks Steam and common emulators — add custom libraries here.
settings.scanner.title: Game scanner
settings.startup.hint: Launches minimized to the system tray so syncing runs in the background.
settings.startup.startOnBoot: Start OpenSave when the computer starts
settings.startup.title: Startup
settings.storage.applyLimits: Apply these limits to every game
settings.storage.applyLimitsHint: Replaces each game's own limits with these, then deletes the snapshots beyond them on every branch. To clean up with each game's own limits, use Space used above.
settings.storage.autoDeleteHint: The snapshots OpenSave takes on its own — before a sync replaces files, when a game saves, at a conflict. Snapshots you took yourself are kept, and so is the newest one on every branch, whatever its age. Runs shortly after start and every few hours.
settings.storage.backupsDirHint: Where version-history snapshots (ZIP archives) are stored.
settings.storage.maxManualSnapshots: Manual snapshots to keep per game
settings.storage.maxManualSnapshotsHint: Snapshots you take yourself have their own budget, so games that auto-save often (Elden Ring, Dragonsword) can't push them out. {keepForever}, which is the default.
settings.storage.maxSnapshots: Automatic snapshots to keep per game
settings.storage.maxSnapshotsHint: Default limit for newly tracked games (0 = keep everything). The oldest are pruned first, per branch. Change a single game's limit in its Configuration tab.
settings.storage.nothingToPrune: Nothing to clean up — all games are within their limit
settings.storage.syncBackupsDirHint: A safety copy of your save is taken here before every incoming sync, so a bad sync is always reversible.
settings.storage.title: Snapshot storage
settings.support.body: It's built and maintained in spare time. If it's saved you the hassle of copying save folders between machines, you're welcome to chip in.
settings.support.foot: Prefer not to donate? Reporting a bug or suggesting a feature helps just as much.
settings.support.lede: Free and open source, and it stays that way — no accounts, no ads, no telemetry, and nothing locked behind a payment.
settings.support.note: Payment is handled entirely by Gumroad — OpenSave never sees your card details.
settings.support.opened: Opened in your browser — thank you.
settings.support.pointFixes: Time for fixes and new features
settings.support.qrCaption:
Scan to pay
from your phone
settings.support.title: Support OpenSave
settings.sync.autoSyncOnTrack: Sync a game immediately when it's first tracked
settings.sync.detectNewGames: Tell me when a game turns up with saves OpenSave isn't keeping
settings.sync.detectNewGamesHint: OpenSave looks every hour, in the background, and only mentions games it hasn't seen before. Nothing is tracked until you choose it.
settings.sync.matchByAppId: Match saves across PCs by Steam App ID
settings.sync.matchByAppIdHint: Links the same game across devices even when it was tracked under different names or drives.
settings.sync.matchByAppIdMore: For example a Steam copy on one PC and a standalone copy on another. Leave this off if you deliberately keep two separate copies of the same game that shouldn't merge. You can always link games by hand from a game's page.
settings.sync.speedLimitHint: Only applies to relay (internet) syncs — LAN is never throttled.
settings.sync.title: Sync behavior
settings.sync.unknownGame: When another device syncs a game this one doesn't have
settings.sync.unknownGameAsk: Ask me where to keep it
settings.sync.unknownGameHint: Tracking automatically works out a folder from where the game lives on the other device, which is why OpenSave usually needs no setup.
settings.sync.unknownGameMore: Choose {askMe} if your saves are somewhere that guess would get wrong — a second drive, a folder you moved, or a game that keeps saves in a folder named after your account. Games waiting for a folder appear on the Home page.
settings.tabs.discordTitle: Open the OpenSave Discord in your browser
settings.title: Settings
settings.updates.betaHint: Betas ship early with the newest fixes and are less tested. You'll be offered the stable release whenever it's newer, so this isn't a one-way door.
settings.updates.onBeta: You're running {version}, which is a beta, so you'll be offered newer betas whether or not this is ticked — otherwise there'd be no way forward until the final release caught up. Untick it and you'll move to the stable release as soon as it's newer than what you have.
settings.updates.title: Updates
settings.usage.deleteConfirm: Delete the {size} snapshot of {game} from {when}?{pinned} This can't be undone; the current save isn't affected.
settings.usage.newestComplete: The newest snapshot of each branch and pinned ones keep complete copies of their own.
settings.usage.pinnedNote: It is pinned, so nothing else would ever have removed it.

settings.usage.sharedSaving: {onDisk} — {saving} less, because older snapshots keep the files they have in common once rather than each keeping its own copy.
settings.usage.sharingExplain: Older snapshots keep the files they have in common once rather than each keeping its own copy, so a game with many save slots doesn't store every slot again in every snapshot.
